title: A Level One Blacksmith In Borrowed Armor Just Wiped Out A Whole Gang . . . (Episode 2)
caption:
Grid is level negative three and can't even afford a carriage ride. Overgeared, episode 2: one epic arrow starts a hunt for the maker, and an old smith's forge becomes a battlefield. Follow for episode 3!

#overgeared #anime #animerecap #animeexplained #fyp
comment: Would you have helped Khan, or kept your arrows and walked away? Why?

segments.say: A level one blacksmith in borrowed *armor* just wiped out an entire gang with one swing.
To see how it got here, go back to the day after the temple *fell*.
Yura won that fight, and the game company is *watching*.
One executive can't stop thinking about the guy who *lost*.
Grid logs back in, and the system says he is now an enemy of the Yatan *cult*.
Worse, he is level negative three, in a town packed with level one hundred *players*.
So he tries to hire a carriage out of there, but the ride costs ten *gold*.
Grid has none. He begs, the driver does not care, and he gets thrown *out*.
Nobody helps a broke man, so Grid pulls himself *together*.
Then it hits him. He is a legendary *blacksmith*, and mastering a few skills lifts every stat ten *percent*.
Better still, he can craft any item he *wants*.
So he designs a greatsword with stats over ten *million*, a meteor on every swing.
And it looks like a *shark*.
Grid stares at it like a proud *father*.
Even the system warns him he went a little *overboard*.
But now he understands how every piece is *made*.
Eighteen hundred attack, before he adds a single *upgrade*.
Feeling good, he walks up to a high level party, and they tell him he can't *join*.
They guess he is level sixty. He says one hundred, and they take it as an *insult*.
Then Ragus, the holy fist, offers to test his *skills*.
Grid takes one look at the shirtless fighter and says *no thanks*.
Smart. He would have lost.
So he begs a village blacksmith to teach him, and the man throws him *out*.
Now Grid is stuck in this village, broke and *hopeless*.
But the smith sees he is still hanging around, and gives him a chore. Chop some *firewood*.
It sounds easy, until his body feels like it will *break*.
Then something odd happens. He is exhausted, yet he does not want to *stop*.
And a new stat unlocks, *fortitude*, which gives him stamina.
By morning he has chopped a thousand *logs*.
The smith is not impressed. Mine me some ore, and *maybe*.
So Grid hauls out huge chunks of ore, in full armor, while the miners just *stare*.
Then he levels up. Grid is finally level *one*, and the penalty is gone.
The smith's trust is now max, so he finally teaches him to make *arrows*.
Yaffa ore melted into steel makes arrows that ignore part of enemy *defense*.
Grid read up on refining before he logged in, and his class fixes the *rest*.
Hard work, plus a cheat code.
He melts the steel, tempers it, and pours everything he has into the *anvil*.
Then a purple glow, and an epic arrow *appears*.
He levels up again, and the smith calls him the second coming of *Pogma*.
So Grid says goodbye and puts his arrows up for *auction*.
Far away, a guild is getting crushed by a stone *golem*.
Their archer buys one of Grid's arrows, and it sells in a *flash*.
She takes one look and freezes. It is *epic*.
She asks the seller who made it, and he has no *idea*.
The furious guild swears to find the maker, and sends word to *everyone*.
Meanwhile, back in the real world, Grid collapses from *exhaustion*.
His parents are worried sick, and his dad slips him some *cash*.
Then Grid counts it out. He earns nine thousand yen a *day*.
But when he checks the auction, his arrows sold for ninety-two *silver* each.
That is more than his whole *paycheck*.
Look out, world. Grid is coming to secure the *bag*.
He rides to Winston Village to find a blacksmith and make *more*.
But the only forge in town is *closed*.
The old smith, Khan, says he had a son Grid's age, but he cannot *help*.
The Merrow Company is buying up his materials, and then its thugs storm *in*.
They tell him to sign the shop away, and that he is the last of his line, now his son is *dead*.
That is cruel, even for a thug.
Khan reminds Grid of his own *grandpa*.
So Grid steps in, and tells the thugs to step *off*.
He hands them a fresh arrow, and a legendary quest *starts*.
It goes badly. His weapon breaks, and Grid is nearly *dead*.

segments.text: Hey, old dude, you want to protect your legacy, right?

segments.say: Khan says yes, so Grid borrows his *gear*.
The thugs laugh. Hide in all the gear you want, you are *fake*.

segments.text: Yeah, I know. And everybody will probably laugh at me.

segments.say: But the only way to get stronger is to be *overgeared*.
One swing, and the whole gang is *wiped out*.
Quest cleared. Grid jumps to level twenty-*one*.
Khan knows who made those weapons. He knew Grid all *along*.
Then Khan hits the floor, and Grid begs him to *stay*.
Far away, a man at dinner hears his mercenaries went *missing*.
He turns to his best killer. Rabbit, it is your *turn*.
